title: Foundational arithmetic dependency catalog
scope: A bounded roadmap of reusable arithmetic facts for Peano Lab. This file records mathematical dependencies and representability; it does not grant theorem authority.

expanded_predicate_conventions.congruent_mod(m,a,b): exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v
expanded_predicate_conventions.div_rem(n,m,q,r): n = m * q + r /\ exists k. k + S r = m
expanded_predicate_conventions.is_gcd(d,a,b): divides(d,a) /\ divides(d,b) /\ forall c. divides(c,a) -> divides(c,b) -> divides(c,d)
expanded_predicate_conventions.prime(p): ~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1
expanded_predicate_conventions.beta_at(b,c,i,x): (exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + x
expanded_predicate_conventions.product(b,c,l,n): exists u v. (((exists h. h + S 1 = S ((S 0) * v)) /\ exists q. u = q * S ((S 0) * v) + 1) /\ (((exists h. h + S n = S ((S l) * v)) /\ exists q. u = q * S ((S l) * v) + n) /\ forall i. (exists h. h + S i = l) -> exists p r s. (((exists h. h + S p = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + p) /\ (((exists h. h + S r = S ((S i) * v)) /\ exists q. u = q * S ((S i) * v) + r) /\ (((exists h. h + S s = S ((S (S i)) * v)) /\ exists q. u = q * S ((S (S i)) * v) + s) /\ s = r * p)))))
expanded_predicate_conventions.all_prime(b,c,l): forall i. (exists h. h + S i = l) -> exists p. (beta_at(b,c,i,p) /\ prime(p))
expanded_predicate_conventions.sorted(b,c,l): forall i. (exists h. h + S (S i) = l) -> exists p q. (beta_at(b,c,i,p) /\ (beta_at(b,c,S i,q) /\ exists h. h + p = q))

statuses.checked_existing: Already present in Peano Lab's theorem ladder and independently kernel-checked.
statuses.checked_m20: Present in the post-baseline arithmetic extension, including compatible upstream modular entries, and independently kernel-checked.
statuses.planned_expressible: Closed formula expressible in today's fixed Peano language, but not yet admitted to the checked runtime library.
statuses.blocked_by_language: A natural reusable statement needs a representation or interface not yet implemented as an expanded Peano target.

companion_artifacts.title: Lean proof of the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
companion_artifacts.scope: Kernel-checked finite-list existence and uniqueness up to permutation for every nonzero natural. This companion is not imported into Peano Lab and does not change any Peano catalog node to checked.

lemmas.title: A successor is not zero
lemmas.summary: Reusable form of Peano axiom PA1.

peano.statement: forall n. ~(S n = 0)

lemmas.title: Successor is injective
lemmas.summary: Reusable form of Peano axiom PA2.

peano.statement: forall n m. S n = S m -> n = m

lemmas.title: Every natural is zero or a successor
lemmas.summary: Constructive case decomposition for naturals, derived by ordinary induction.

peano.statement: forall n. n = 0 \/ exists k. n = S k

lemmas.title: Every nonzero natural has a predecessor
lemmas.summary: Extracts a predecessor constructively without double-negation elimination.

peano.statement: forall n. ~(n = 0) -> exists k. n = S k

lemmas.title: Equality is symmetric
lemmas.summary: Packages the primitive symmetry rule as a reusable universally quantified fact.

peano.statement: forall a b. a = b -> b = a

lemmas.summary: Packages the primitive transitivity rule for downstream rewriting arguments.

peano.statement: forall a b c. a = b -> b = c -> a = c

peano.statement: forall a b. a = b -> S a = S b

lemmas.summary: The binary addition congruence rule in reusable closed form.

peano.statement: forall a b c d. a = b -> c = d -> a + c = b + d

lemmas.summary: The binary multiplication congruence rule in reusable closed form.

peano.statement: forall a b c d. a = b -> c = d -> a * c = b * d

lemmas.title: Equality of naturals is decidable
lemmas.summary: Nested induction constructs either an equality proof or a refutation for every pair of naturals.

peano.statement: forall a b. a = b \/ ~(a = b)

lemmas.title: Zero is a left identity for addition
lemmas.summary: The induction-derived orientation complementary to PA3.

peano.statement: forall n. 0 + n = n

peano.statement: forall n m. S n + m = S (n + m)

lemmas.summary: The first substantial induction theorem in the arithmetic ladder.

peano.statement: forall n m. n + m = m + n

lemmas.title: Addition is associative
lemmas.summary: The reassociation law used throughout order and divisibility proofs.

peano.statement: forall n m k. (n + m) + k = n + (m + k)

lemmas.title: The outer terms of two additive pairs may be permuted
lemmas.summary: Permute the outer entries of two additive pairs.

peano.statement: forall a b c d. (a + b) + (c + d) = (c + b) + (a + d)

lemmas.title: A zero sum has a zero right summand
lemmas.summary: Extracts the right component from a sum equal to zero.

peano.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> b = 0

lemmas.title: Adding a positive successor has no fixed point
lemmas.summary: A positivity helper expressed without a primitive strict-order relation.

peano.statement: forall p n. S p + n = n -> false

lemmas.title: Drop an additive prefix from a fixed-point equation
lemmas.summary: Helper underlying additive-witness antisymmetry.

peano.statement: forall a b n. (b + a) + n = n -> a + n = n

lemmas.title: Addition cancels on the right
lemmas.summary: A core cancellation lemma for order, congruence, and divisibility.

peano.statement: forall a b c. a + c = b + c -> a = b

lemmas.title: Addition cancels on the left
lemmas.summary: The commuted cancellation orientation.

peano.statement: forall a b c. a + b = a + c -> b = c

lemmas.title: A zero sum has a zero left summand
lemmas.summary: The symmetric component of zero-sum elimination.

peano.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> a = 0

lemmas.title: Both summands of a zero sum are zero
lemmas.summary: Combines both useful projections into one conjunction.

peano.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> a = 0 /\ b = 0

lemmas.title: Zero is a left annihilator for multiplication
lemmas.summary: The induction-derived orientation complementary to PA5.

peano.statement: forall n. 0 * n = 0

lemmas.title: Successor moves through multiplication on the left
lemmas.summary: The left-oriented successor multiplication law.

peano.statement: forall n m. S n * m = n * m + m

lemmas.title: Multiplication is commutative
lemmas.summary: Commutativity derived by induction from both successor orientations.

peano.statement: forall n m. n * m = m * n

lemmas.title: Multiplication distributes over right addition
lemmas.summary: The right-distributive orientation used by multiplication associativity.

peano.statement: forall n m k. n * (m + k) = n * m + n * k

lemmas.title: Multiplication is associative
lemmas.summary: The multiplication reassociation law.

peano.statement: forall n m k. (n * m) * k = n * (m * k)

lemmas.title: One is a left identity for multiplication
lemmas.summary: The induction-derived left identity orientation.

peano.statement: forall n. 1 * n = n

lemmas.title: One is a right identity for multiplication
lemmas.summary: The right identity orientation used by divisibility reflexivity.

peano.statement: forall n. n * 1 = n

lemmas.title: Left addition distributes through multiplication
lemmas.summary: The left-distributive orientation completing the commutative-semiring basis.

peano.statement: forall n m k. (n + m) * k = n * k + m * k

lemmas.title: A zero product has a zero factor
lemmas.summary: The current theorem-ladder capstone.

peano.statement: forall n m. n * m = 0 -> n = 0 \/ m = 0

lemmas.title: A product of nonzero naturals is nonzero
lemmas.summary: The contrapositive-facing form of the checked zero-product theorem.

lemmas.title: A left factor of a nonzero product is nonzero
lemmas.summary: Substitution of a hypothetical zero factor contradicts the product's nonzero hypothesis.

peano.statement: forall n c d. ~(n = 0) -> n = c * d -> ~(c = 0)

lemmas.title: Two is not a product of two successors of successors
lemmas.summary: The bounded factor obstruction used by the checked proof that two is prime.

peano.statement: forall a b. ~(2 = S (S a) * S (S b))

lemmas.title: Both factors of a product equal to one are one
lemmas.summary: A basic unit-factor lemma needed by the expanded prime predicate.

peano.statement: forall a b. a * b = 1 -> a = 1 /\ b = 1

lemmas.title: A nonzero factor cancels on the left
lemmas.summary: Cancellation with the natural-number nonzero side condition made explicit.

peano.statement: forall a b c. ~(a = 0) -> a * b = a * c -> b = c

lemmas.title: A nonzero factor cancels on the right
lemmas.summary: Reduces right cancellation to the checked left-cancellation theorem by commutativity.

peano.statement: forall a b c. ~(c = 0) -> a * c = b * c -> a = b

lemmas.title: Left multiplication preserves order
lemmas.summary: Multiplies the explicit order witness and distributes the common left factor.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + c * a = c * b

lemmas.title: Right multiplication preserves order
lemmas.summary: Multiplies the explicit order witness and distributes the common right factor.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + a * c = b * c

lemmas.title: A nonzero left factor strictly separates successor products
lemmas.summary: Constructs the strict-order witness for c*a below c*(a+1) when c is nonzero.

peano.statement: forall c a. ~(c = 0) -> exists r. r + S (c * a) = c * S a

lemmas.title: Order is reflexive
lemmas.summary: Uses zero as the additive witness for the expanded order relation.

peano.statement: forall n. exists k. k + n = n

lemmas.title: Order is transitive
lemmas.summary: Composes two additive order witnesses.

peano.statement: forall n m k. (exists a. a + n = m) -> (exists b. b + m = k) -> exists c. c + n = k

lemmas.title: Opposing additive witnesses force equality
lemmas.summary: The additive core of order antisymmetry.

peano.statement: forall a b n m. a + n = m -> b + m = n -> n = m

lemmas.title: Order is antisymmetric
lemmas.summary: Eliminates the two existential order witnesses through the checked helper.

peano.statement: forall n m. (exists a. a + n = m) -> (exists b. b + m = n) -> n = m

lemmas.title: Natural-number order is total
lemmas.summary: Every pair of naturals has an additive witness in one direction.

peano.statement: forall n m. (exists a. a + n = m) \/ exists b. b + m = n

lemmas.title: Zero is below every natural number
lemmas.summary: The number itself supplies the expanded additive witness.

peano.statement: forall n. exists k. k + 0 = n

lemmas.title: Every natural is below its successor
lemmas.summary: One supplies the expanded additive witness.

peano.statement: forall n. exists k. k + n = S n

lemmas.title: Only zero lies below zero
lemmas.summary: Eliminates an additive witness ending at zero.

peano.statement: forall n. (exists k. k + n = 0) -> n = 0

lemmas.title: Every nonzero natural is at least one
lemmas.summary: Ordinary induction supplies the predecessor as the additive order witness.

peano.statement: forall n. ~(n = 0) -> exists k. k + 1 = n

lemmas.title: A natural at least one is nonzero
lemmas.summary: A hypothetical equality with zero would force the successor one to equal zero.

peano.statement: forall n. (exists k. k + 1 = n) -> ~(n = 0)

lemmas.title: A number is below a left-added summand
lemmas.summary: The added term itself is already the expanded order witness.

peano.statement: forall a b. exists k. k + a = b + a

lemmas.title: A number is below itself plus a right summand
lemmas.summary: The right summand becomes the additive order witness after commutation.

peano.statement: forall a b. exists k. k + a = a + b

lemmas.title: Adding the same right summand preserves order
lemmas.summary: Transports an explicit additive witness through right addition.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + (a + c) = b + c

lemmas.title: Adding the same left summand preserves order
lemmas.summary: Reassociates and commutes an explicit order witness through left addition.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + (c + a) = c + b

lemmas.title: Successor preserves order
lemmas.summary: Transports an additive order witness through successor using PA4.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + S a = S b

lemmas.title: Successor reflects order
lemmas.summary: Cancels successor from both sides of an explicit additive order witness.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + S a = S b) -> exists r. r + a = b

lemmas.title: Order is preserved by raising the upper bound
lemmas.summary: Turns the witness k into S k when the upper bound is replaced by its successor.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> exists r. r + a = S b

lemmas.title: Strict order entails weak order
lemmas.summary: Absorbs the successor from the lower term into the additive witness.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> exists r. r + a = b

lemmas.title: Cancel a common right summand from order
lemmas.summary: Reassociates the witness equation and applies equality cancellation.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + (a + c) = b + c) -> exists r. r + a = b

lemmas.title: Strict order is irreflexive
lemmas.summary: Uses S n <= n as the fixed-language expansion of n < n.

peano.statement: forall n. ~ (exists k. k + S n = n)

lemmas.title: A weak inequality is equality or strict inequality
lemmas.summary: Decomposes the additive order witness constructively into zero and successor cases.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> a = b \/ exists k. k + S a = b

lemmas.title: Strict order followed by weak order
lemmas.summary: Applies weak-order transitivity with the successor lower endpoint.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> (exists k. k + b = c) -> exists k. k + S a = c

lemmas.title: Weak order followed by strict order
lemmas.summary: Composes the two additive witnesses directly to avoid proof-tree duplication.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + a = b) -> (exists k. k + S b = c) -> exists k. k + S a = c

lemmas.title: Strict order is transitive
lemmas.summary: Combines strict additive witnesses and transports their successor explicitly.

peano.statement: forall a b c. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> (exists k. k + S b = c) -> exists k. k + S a = c

lemmas.title: Weak-or-reverse-strict comparison
lemmas.summary: Decomposes the reverse total-order witness into zero and successor cases.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) \/ exists k. k + S b = a

lemmas.title: Natural strict-order trichotomy
lemmas.summary: Splits the total-order witness constructively into equality or one of two strict directions.

peano.statement: forall a b. a = b \/ ((exists k. k + S a = b) \/ exists k. k + S b = a)

lemmas.title: Strict order excludes reverse weak order
lemmas.summary: A direct descent argument rejects opposing additive witnesses constructively.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + S a = b) -> ~(exists k. k + b = a)

lemmas.title: Weak order excludes reverse strict order
lemmas.summary: Applies strict-versus-weak incompatibility in the reverse orientation.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists k. k + a = b) -> ~(exists k. k + S b = a)

lemmas.title: A strict bound cannot occur inside an additive decomposition of the lower term
lemmas.summary: The strengthened direct descent shape is the compact contradiction bridge used by division uniqueness.

peano.statement: forall r m a b. (exists k. k + S r = m) -> ~(r = (a + m) + b)

lemmas.title: Divisibility is reflexive
lemmas.summary: Uses one as the expanded divisibility witness.

peano.statement: forall a. exists k. a = a * k

lemmas.title: One divides every natural number
lemmas.summary: The target number is the divisibility witness.

peano.statement: forall a. exists k. a = 1 * k

lemmas.title: Every natural number divides zero
lemmas.summary: Zero supplies the divisibility witness through PA5.

peano.statement: forall a. exists k. 0 = a * k

lemmas.title: Divisibility is transitive
lemmas.summary: Multiplies two explicit witnesses.

peano.statement: forall a b n. (exists q. n = a * q) -> (exists r. a = b * r) -> exists s. n = b * s

lemmas.title: A common divisor divides a sum
lemmas.summary: Adds the two divisibility witnesses and distributes.

peano.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> (exists r. m = a * r) -> exists s. n + m = a * s

lemmas.title: A divisor remains a divisor after right multiplication
lemmas.summary: Extends a witness by multiplying it with the new factor.

peano.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> exists s. n * m = a * s

lemmas.title: A divisor remains a divisor after left multiplication
lemmas.summary: The commuted multiplication closure for explicit multiple witnesses.

peano.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> exists s. m * n = a * s

lemmas.title: The right factor divides a product
lemmas.summary: Commutativity supplies the explicit witness that the right factor divides a product.

peano.statement: forall a b. exists k. a * b = b * k

lemmas.title: A bounded common multiple extends by one
lemmas.summary: Multiplying a nonzero common multiple through a bound by the new positive endpoint extends its divisibility property to the successor bound.

peano.statement: forall B c. ~(c = 0) -> (forall t. (exists h. S t + S h = S B) -> exists k. c = S t * k) -> exists c2. (~(c2 = 0) /\ forall t. (exists h. S t + S h = S (S B)) -> exists k. c2 = S t * k)

lemmas.title: Every finite initial interval has a nonzero common multiple
lemmas.summary: Ordinary induction constructs a nonzero natural divisible by every positive natural in the encoded finite initial interval.

peano.statement: forall B. exists c. (~(c = 0) /\ forall t. (exists h. S t + S h = S B) -> exists k. c = S t * k)

lemmas.title: A divisor of a nonzero natural is bounded
lemmas.summary: Extracts a positive quotient and expands it as a successor to construct the order witness.

peano.statement: forall d n. ~(n = 0) -> (exists q. n = d * q) -> exists k. k + d = n

lemmas.title: Every divisor of one is one
lemmas.summary: Applies the checked factor-of-one theorem to the explicit divisibility witness.

peano.statement: forall d. (exists y. 1 = d * y) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: Divisibility is antisymmetric
lemmas.summary: Handles the zero case directly; otherwise cancellation turns the two divisibility witnesses into a unit product.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists x. b = a * x) -> (exists y. a = b * y) -> a = b

lemmas.title: A common-factor difference retains the factor
lemmas.summary: Induction on both factor witnesses and additive cancellation construct a witness for the residual multiple.

peano.statement: forall c u v r. c * u = c * v + r -> exists w. r = c * w

lemmas.title: A common divisor divides a Euclidean remainder
lemmas.summary: Reassociates the divisor multiple inside a quotient block and applies the checked factor-difference theorem.

peano.statement: forall c a b q r. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> a = b * q + r -> exists w. r = c * w

lemmas.title: A common divisor divides a Euclidean linear step
lemmas.summary: Combines the two explicit multiple witnesses by associativity and right distributivity.

peano.statement: forall c b q r. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. r = c * v) -> exists w. b * q + r = c * w

lemmas.title: A nonmultiple differs from every candidate multiple
lemmas.summary: Moves existential negation to a reusable pointwise family without classical logic.

peano.statement: forall a n. ~(exists q. n = a * q) -> forall q. ~(n = a * q)

lemmas.title: Pointwise inequality excludes every multiple witness
lemmas.summary: Reconstructs existential negation from the pointwise family.

peano.statement: forall a n. (forall q. ~(n = a * q)) -> ~(exists q. n = a * q)

lemmas.title: Balanced natural congruence is reflexive
lemmas.summary: Uses the balanced existential definition that avoids integer subtraction.

peano.statement: forall m a. exists u v. a + m * u = a + m * v

lemmas.title: Balanced natural congruence is symmetric
lemmas.summary: Swaps both existential witnesses and reverses the equality.

peano.statement: forall m a b. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> exists r s. b + m * r = a + m * s

lemmas.title: Balanced natural congruence is transitive
lemmas.summary: Combines balanced witnesses without introducing subtraction.

peano.statement: forall m a b c. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> (exists r s. b + m * r = c + m * s) -> exists x y. a + m * x = c + m * y

lemmas.title: Balanced congruence respects addition
lemmas.summary: Adds two congruences using combined balanced witnesses.

peano.statement: forall m a b c d. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> (exists r s. c + m * r = d + m * s) -> exists x y. (a + c) + m * x = (b + d) + m * y

lemmas.title: Balanced congruence is stable under right multiplication
lemmas.summary: Multiplies a balanced witness equation and reassociates its modulus factors.

peano.statement: forall m a b c. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> exists r s. (a * c) + m * r = (b * c) + m * s

lemmas.title: Balanced congruence is stable under left multiplication
lemmas.summary: Derives left scaling from right scaling and multiplication commutativity.

peano.statement: forall m a b c. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> exists r s. (c * a) + m * r = (c * b) + m * s

lemmas.title: Balanced congruence respects multiplication
lemmas.summary: Scales the two input congruences on opposite sides and composes them transitively.

peano.statement: forall m a b c d. (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> (exists r s. c + m * r = d + m * s) -> exists x y. (a * c) + m * x = (b * d) + m * y

lemmas.title: A quotient-remainder decomposition gives congruence
lemmas.summary: Turns a directed equation b = qm + x into the balanced relation b congruent to x modulo m.

peano.statement: forall m b q x. b = q * m + x -> exists u v. b + m * u = x + m * v

lemmas.title: A multiple is congruent to zero
lemmas.summary: Connects expanded divisibility with the balanced modular relation.

peano.statement: forall m a. (exists k. a = m * k) -> exists u v. a + m * u = 0 + m * v

lemmas.title: Absorb a known residue decomposition into a multiple
lemmas.summary: A general quotient-update identity used by residue calculations.

peano.statement: forall a u c r s. r = a * c + s -> a * u + r = a * (u + c) + s

lemmas.title: Lift an additive residue decomposition
lemmas.summary: Combines a decomposed input with a decomposed residue and returns the updated quotient.

peano.statement: forall a x u r q t c s. x = a * q + t -> r + t = a * c + s -> (a * u + r) + x = a * ((u + q) + c) + s

lemmas.title: Expand the square of a quotient-residue decomposition
lemmas.summary: The generic algebraic decomposition behind reusable square-residue arguments.

peano.statement: forall a z q r. z = a * q + r -> z * z = a * (q * z + r * q) + r * r

lemmas.title: Lift a residue decomposition through squaring
lemmas.summary: Combines a decomposition of z with a decomposition of its residue square.

peano.statement: forall a z q r c s. z = a * q + r -> r * r = a * c + s -> z * z = a * ((q * z + r * q) + c) + s

lemmas.title: Package a square residue as an existential witness
lemmas.summary: Forgets the explicit quotient formula while retaining a reusable existential multiple witness.

peano.statement: forall a z q r c s. z = a * q + r -> r * r = a * c + s -> exists w. z * z = a * w + s

lemmas.title: Regroup a fourth power as a square of a square
lemmas.summary: Associativity exposes the square-of-a-square form used by residue proofs.

peano.statement: forall n. n * n * n * n = (n * n) * (n * n)

lemmas.title: Every natural has one of five residues modulo five
lemmas.summary: A checked induction partitions every natural into the five explicit quotient-and-remainder cases.

peano.statement: forall n. exists q. n = 5 * q \/ n = 5 * q + 1 \/ n = 5 * q + 2 \/ n = 5 * q + 3 \/ n = 5 * q + 4

lemmas.title: A nonmultiple of five has a nonzero residue
lemmas.summary: The zero-residue branch contradicts the nonmultiple hypothesis, leaving four cases.

peano.statement: forall n. ~(exists q. n = 5 * q) -> exists q. n = 5 * q + 1 \/ n = 5 * q + 2 \/ n = 5 * q + 3 \/ n = 5 * q + 4

lemmas.title: Squaring residue one modulo five preserves residue one
lemmas.summary: An explicit quotient witnesses that the square of 5q+1 again has remainder one.

peano.statement: forall z q. z = 5 * q + 1 -> z * z = 5 * (q * z + q) + 1

lemmas.title: Squaring residue two modulo five gives residue four
lemmas.summary: An explicit quotient witnesses that the square of 5q+2 has remainder four.

peano.statement: forall z q. z = 5 * q + 2 -> z * z = 5 * ((q * z + q) + q) + 4

lemmas.title: Squaring residue three modulo five gives residue four
lemmas.summary: The generic square-residue lift computes the residue-three case.

lemmas.title: Squaring residue four modulo five gives residue one
lemmas.summary: The generic square-residue lift computes the residue-four case.

lemmas.title: Fourth powers preserve residue one modulo five
lemmas.summary: Squaring the residue-one square yields an explicit fourth-power witness.

lemmas.title: Fourth powers of residue two are one modulo five
lemmas.summary: The residue-two square has residue four, whose square has residue one.

lemmas.title: Fourth powers of residue three are one modulo five
lemmas.summary: The residue-three square has residue four, whose square has residue one.

lemmas.title: Fourth powers of residue four are one modulo five
lemmas.summary: The residue-four square has residue one, whose square stays residue one.

lemmas.title: A nonmultiple of five has fourth power one modulo five
lemmas.summary: The original residue theorem is now an ordinary imported, replayed, empty-context kernel theorem.

peano.statement: forall n. ~(exists x. n = 5 * x) -> exists x. n * n * n * n = 5 * x + 1

lemmas.title: Division with remainder for successor divisors
lemmas.summary: Constructive induction on the dividend, splitting the remainder-gap witness into zero and successor cases.

peano.statement: forall d n. exists q r. n = S d * q + r /\ exists k. k + S r = S d

lemmas.title: Division with remainder for every nonzero divisor
lemmas.summary: Extracts a predecessor from the nonzero divisor and applies the successor-divisor construction.

peano.statement: forall m n. ~(m = 0) -> exists q r. n = m * q + r /\ exists k. k + S r = m

lemmas.title: Advance a strict remainder bound by one step
lemmas.summary: Specializes the checked equality-or-strict decomposition to the successor of a remainder.

peano.statement: forall r d. (exists k. k + S r = d) -> S r = d \/ exists k. k + S (S r) = d

lemmas.title: A bounded remainder lies below the next divisor block
lemmas.summary: Rearranges the explicit remainder-bound witness into a strict upper block bound without subtraction.

peano.statement: forall d q r. (exists k. k + S r = d) -> exists k. k + S (d * q + r) = d * S q

lemmas.title: A positive quotient gap contradicts bounded remainders
lemmas.summary: Expands the larger quotient, cancels the common block, and contradicts the smaller remainder bound.

peano.statement: forall m q q2 r s k. (exists z. z + S r = m) -> S k + q = q2 -> ~(m * q + r = m * q2 + s)

lemmas.title: Remainders are unique at a fixed quotient
lemmas.summary: Cancels the common divisor-times-quotient prefix.

peano.statement: forall d q r s. d * q + r = d * q + s -> r = s

lemmas.title: Quotient and remainder are unique
lemmas.summary: Totality splits the quotient gap; zero gives equality and cancellation, while a positive gap contradicts one strict remainder bound.

peano.statement: forall m n q r q2 r2. n = m * q + r -> (exists k. k + S r = m) -> n = m * q2 + r2 -> (exists k. k + S r2 = m) -> q = q2 /\ r = r2

lemmas.title: Bounded congruent representatives are equal
lemmas.summary: Views a balanced congruence as two bounded remainder decompositions of one natural and applies remainder uniqueness.

peano.statement: forall m a b. (exists ha. ha + S a = m) -> (exists hb. hb + S b = m) -> (exists u v. a + m * u = b + m * v) -> a = b

lemmas.title: A bounded congruent representative is a directed remainder
lemmas.summary: Divides the code, proves its canonical remainder congruent to the proposed bounded value, and identifies them by uniqueness.

peano.statement: forall m b x. ~(m = 0) -> (exists h. h + S x = m) -> (exists u v. b + m * u = x + m * v) -> exists q. b = q * m + x

lemmas.title: Balanced Bézout identity projected modulo the left modulus
lemmas.summary: Reorders a balanced Bézout identity to expose the coefficient of the right modulus as a modular inverse modulo the left modulus.

peano.statement: forall m n xp yp xn yn. m * xp + n * yp = 1 + (m * xn + n * yn) -> exists u v. n * yp + m * u = (1 + n * yn) + m * v

lemmas.title: Balanced Bézout identity projected modulo the right modulus
lemmas.summary: Reassociates a balanced Bézout identity to expose the coefficient of the left modulus as a modular inverse modulo the right modulus.

peano.statement: forall m n xp yp xn yn. m * xp + n * yp = 1 + (m * xn + n * yn) -> exists u v. m * xp + n * u = (1 + m * xn) + n * v

lemmas.title: Successor-predecessor cancellation in balanced congruence
lemmas.summary: Implements subtraction of one modulo a successor using only natural addition and multiplication.

peano.statement: forall k a z. exists u v. ((a + z) + k * z) + S k * u = a + S k * v

lemmas.title: Zero remainder implies divisibility
lemmas.summary: Erases the definitional zero addend and returns the quotient as a divisibility witness.

peano.statement: forall m n q. n = m * q + 0 -> exists k. n = m * k

lemmas.title: A multiple has a bounded zero remainder
lemmas.summary: For a nonzero divisor, packages its divisibility witness as a quotient-remainder decomposition with remainder zero.

peano.statement: forall m n. ~(m = 0) -> (exists q. n = m * q) -> exists q r. (n = m * q + r /\ r = 0) /\ exists k. k + S r = m

lemmas.title: Divisibility by a nonzero natural is decidable
lemmas.summary: A checked quotient-remainder decomposition decides divisibility by testing whether its unique remainder is zero.

peano.statement: forall d n. ~(d = 0) -> (exists q. n = d * q) \/ ~(exists q. n = d * q)

lemmas.title: Divisibility of naturals is decidable
lemmas.summary: The nonzero-divisor decision extends constructively across the explicit zero-divisor case.

peano.statement: forall d n. (exists q. n = d * q) \/ ~(exists q. n = d * q)

lemmas.title: Every natural is the gcd of itself and zero
lemmas.summary: Reflexive divisibility and divisibility of zero supply the two witnesses; greatestness is the left common-divisor premise.

peano.statement: forall a. (((exists x. a = a * x) /\ (exists y. 0 = a * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. 0 = c * v) -> exists w. a = c * w)

lemmas.title: The relational gcd specification is symmetric
lemmas.summary: Swaps the two divisibility witnesses and the common-divisor premises in the fully expanded IsGCD relation.

peano.statement: forall g a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> ((exists x. b = g * x) /\ (exists y. a = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. a = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w

lemmas.title: A relational gcd divides the left input
lemmas.summary: Projects the first divisibility witness from the fully expanded IsGCD relation.

peano.statement: forall g a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> exists x. a = g * x

lemmas.title: A relational gcd divides the right input
lemmas.summary: Projects the second divisibility witness from the fully expanded IsGCD relation.

peano.statement: forall g a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> exists y. b = g * y

lemmas.title: Every common divisor divides a relational gcd
lemmas.summary: Projects and specializes the greatestness clause of the fully expanded IsGCD relation.

peano.statement: forall g a b c. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall d. (exists u. a = d * u) -> (exists v. b = d * v) -> exists w. g = d * w) -> (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w

lemmas.title: A divisor is the gcd of itself and its multiple
lemmas.summary: Uses reflexive divisibility and returns each common-divisor witness of the left input as the greatestness witness.

peano.statement: forall a b. (exists y. b = a * y) -> (((exists x. a = a * x) /\ (exists y. b = a * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. a = c * w)

lemmas.title: The relational greatest common divisor is unique
lemmas.summary: Each greatestness clause makes the other gcd divide it, after which divisibility antisymmetry identifies the two witnesses.

peano.statement: forall g h a b. (((exists x. a = g * x) /\ (exists y. b = g * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. g = c * w) -> (((exists x. a = h * x) /\ (exists y. b = h * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. h = c * w) -> g = h

lemmas.title: Euclidean gcd invariance in the forward direction
lemmas.summary: For a = b*q+r, a gcd of b and r divides a, while each common divisor of a and b divides r.

peano.statement: forall d a b q r. a = b * q + r -> (((exists x. b = d * x) /\ (exists y. r = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. r = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w) -> (((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w)

lemmas.title: Euclidean gcd invariance in the backward direction
lemmas.summary: For a = b*q+r, a gcd of a and b divides r, while each common divisor of b and r divides a.

peano.statement: forall d a b q r. a = b * q + r -> (((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w) -> (((exists x. b = d * x) /\ (exists y. r = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. r = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w)

lemmas.title: A greatest common divisor exists below a fixed bound
lemmas.summary: Bounded induction constructs a relational gcd whenever the right input is at most the bound.

peano.statement: forall B b. (exists t. t + b = B) -> forall a. exists d. (((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w)

lemmas.title: A greatest common divisor exists
lemmas.summary: Every pair of naturals has a relational greatest common divisor.

peano.statement: forall a b. exists d. (((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w)

lemmas.title: Coprimality is symmetric
lemmas.summary: Swaps the two common-divisor hypotheses in the expanded relational definition.

peano.statement: forall a b. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> forall c. (exists u. b = c * u) -> (exists v. a = c * v) -> c = 1

lemmas.title: Every natural number is coprime to one
lemmas.summary: Any divisor of one must itself be one.

peano.statement: forall a d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. 1 = d * y) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: One is coprime to every natural number
lemmas.summary: The left-oriented expanded coprimality statement also reduces to the divisor-of-one theorem.

peano.statement: forall a d. (exists x. 1 = d * x) -> (exists y. a = d * y) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: Coprimality constructs a relational gcd equal to one
lemmas.summary: Packages the two one-divisibility witnesses and turns each common divisor equality into a divisor-of-one witness.

peano.statement: forall a b. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> (((exists x. a = 1 * x) /\ (exists y. b = 1 * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. 1 = c * w)

lemmas.title: A relational gcd equal to one implies coprimality
lemmas.summary: Projects the greatestness clause and applies the divisor-of-one theorem to each common divisor.

peano.statement: forall a b. (((exists x. a = 1 * x) /\ (exists y. b = 1 * y)) /\ forall d. (exists u. a = d * u) -> (exists v. b = d * v) -> exists w. 1 = d * w) -> forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> c = 1

lemmas.title: Balanced Bézout coefficients cross one Euclidean step
lemmas.summary: Transport balanced natural Bezout coefficients across one Euclidean division step.

peano.statement: forall a b q r d xp yp xn yn. a = b * q + r -> b * xp + r * yp = d + (b * xn + r * yn) -> a * yp + b * (xp + q * yn) = d + (a * yn + b * (xn + q * yp))

lemmas.title: A gcd with balanced Bézout witnesses exists below a bound
lemmas.summary: Bounded Euclidean descent simultaneously constructs a relational gcd and balanced natural Bezout witnesses.

peano.statement: forall B b. (exists t. t + b = B) -> forall a. exists d. ((((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w) /\ exists xp yp xn yn. a * xp + b * yp = d + (a * xn + b * yn))

lemmas.title: A gcd has balanced natural Bézout coefficients
lemmas.summary: Every pair has a relational gcd together with balanced natural Bezout witnesses.

peano.statement: forall a b. exists d. ((((exists x. a = d * x) /\ (exists y. b = d * y)) /\ forall c. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> exists w. d = c * w) /\ exists xp yp xn yn. a * xp + b * yp = d + (a * xn + b * yn))

lemmas.title: A balanced combination may be scaled on the right
lemmas.summary: Scale a balanced natural combination on the right.

peano.statement: forall a b d xp yp xn yn z. a * xp + b * yp = d + (a * xn + b * yn) -> a * (xp * z) + (b * z) * yp = d * z + (a * (xn * z) + (b * z) * yn)

lemmas.title: A common divisor divides a balanced-combination result
lemmas.summary: Every common divisor of two inputs divides the result of a balanced natural combination.

peano.statement: forall c a b d xp yp xn yn. (exists u. a = c * u) -> (exists v. b = c * v) -> a * xp + b * yp = d + (a * xn + b * yn) -> exists w. d = c * w

lemmas.title: Coprime inputs have a balanced Bézout identity
lemmas.summary: Coprime inputs admit balanced natural Bezout coefficients with result one.

peano.statement: forall a b. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> exists xp yp xn yn. a * xp + b * yp = 1 + (a * xn + b * yn)

lemmas.title: Gauss cancellation for coprime factors
lemmas.summary: Cancel a coprime factor from a divisibility witness (Gauss cancellation).

peano.statement: forall a b z. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> (exists q. b * z = a * q) -> exists w. z = a * w

lemmas.title: Coprimality is closed under multiplication on the left
lemmas.summary: A common divisor of a product and the fixed right operand inherits coprimality with the first factor; Gauss cancellation then makes it divide the second factor.

peano.statement: forall a b n. (forall d. (exists x. a = d * x) -> (exists y. n = d * y) -> d = 1) -> (forall d. (exists x. b = d * x) -> (exists y. n = d * y) -> d = 1) -> forall d. (exists x. a * b = d * x) -> (exists y. n = d * y) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: Coprimality is closed under multiplication on the right
lemmas.summary: The symmetric fixed-left form follows from product coprimality and symmetry of the expanded common-divisor relation.

peano.statement: forall n a b. (forall d. (exists x. n = d * x) -> (exists y. a = d * y) -> d = 1) -> (forall d. (exists x. n = d * x) -> (exists y. b = d * y) -> d = 1) -> forall d. (exists x. n = d * x) -> (exists y. a * b = d * y) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: Congruence descends along modulus divisibility
lemmas.summary: If m divides P, balanced congruence modulo P supplies balanced congruence modulo m by multiplying both witnesses by the quotient.

peano.statement: forall m P x a. (exists k. P = m * k) -> (exists u v. x + P * u = a + P * v) -> exists r s. x + m * r = a + m * s

lemmas.title: Constructive binary Chinese remainder theorem
lemmas.summary: Constructs one natural satisfying two balanced congruences for arbitrary residues and positive coprime moduli, using balanced natural Bézout witnesses and predecessor cancellation instead of integer subtraction.

peano.statement: forall m n a b. ~(m = 0) -> ~(n = 0) -> (forall d. (exists u. m = d * u) -> (exists v. n = d * v) -> d = 1) -> exists x. (exists u v. x + m * u = a + m * v) /\ (exists r s. x + n * r = b + n * s)

lemmas.title: Binary CRT with directed remainder witnesses
lemmas.summary: Converts the two balanced congruences from binary CRT into quotient-and-remainder equations when both requested residues are bounded.

peano.statement: forall m n a b. ~(m = 0) -> ~(n = 0) -> (forall d. (exists u. m = d * u) -> (exists v. n = d * v) -> d = 1) -> (exists ha. ha + S a = m) -> (exists hb. hb + S b = n) -> exists x q r. (x = q * m + a /\ x = r * n + b)

lemmas.title: One CRT fold step preserves all accumulated congruences
lemmas.summary: Extending an accumulated product modulus by one coprime nonzero modulus preserves every old congruence whose modulus divides the product and adds the requested new congruence.

peano.statement: forall P n x b. ~(P = 0) -> ~(n = 0) -> (forall d. (exists u. P = d * u) -> (exists v. n = d * v) -> d = 1) -> exists z. ((forall m a. (exists k. P = m * k) -> (exists u v. x + m * u = a + m * v) -> exists r s. z + m * r = a + m * s) /\ exists q r. z + n * q = b + n * r)

lemmas.title: Bézout identity with integer coefficients
lemmas.summary: The conventional reusable theorem quantifies over signed coefficients.

blocker.detail: Peano Lab quantifies only over naturals and has no integer encoding or subtraction. A balanced natural reformulation is possible, but it is a different interface and should be designed explicitly.
unblocks_with: or a separately named balanced-natural Bézout relation

lemmas.title: Two is prime
lemmas.summary: First concrete theorem using the fully expanded natural prime predicate.

lemmas.title: Three is prime
lemmas.summary: A second concrete prime proof for the numerical and factorization toolkit.

lemmas.title: A bounded factor property extends across one boundary
lemmas.summary: Splits a factor bounded by a successor into the old bounded range or the newly added endpoint.

peano.statement: forall B n. (forall c d. (exists k. k + c = B) -> n = c * d -> c = 1 \/ d = 1) -> (forall d. n = S B * d -> S B = 1 \/ d = 1) -> forall c d. (exists k. k + c = S B) -> n = c * d -> c = 1 \/ d = 1

lemmas.title: Bounded nontrivial factor search
lemmas.summary: Induction on the bound either verifies every bounded factor pair has a unit or returns an explicit nontrivial pair.

peano.statement: forall B n. ~(n = 0) -> ((forall c d. (exists k. k + c = B) -> n = c * d -> c = 1 \/ d = 1) \/ exists c d. ((((exists k. k + c = B) /\ ~(c = 1)) /\ ~(d = 1)) /\ n = c * d))

lemmas.title: Every nontrivial natural is prime or composite
lemmas.summary: Checked bounded search either verifies the expanded prime predicate or constructs a nontrivial factor pair.

lemmas.title: Every prime natural is nonzero
lemmas.summary: The factorization of zero as zero times zero contradicts its expanded prime factor-pair property.

peano.statement: forall p. (~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1) -> ~(p = 0)

lemmas.title: Primality of naturals is decidable
lemmas.summary: Equality tests isolate zero and one; constructive prime-or-composite search decides every remaining natural.

peano.statement: forall n. ((~(n = 1) /\ forall a b. n = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1) \/ ~((~(n = 1) /\ forall a b. n = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1)))

lemmas.title: A proper factor is strictly smaller than its product
lemmas.summary: A bounded factor is either strict or equal to the product; equality and cancellation would force the cofactor to be one.

peano.statement: forall n c d. ~(n = 0) -> n = c * d -> ~(d = 1) -> exists k. k + S c = n

lemmas.title: Bounded prime-divisor existence
lemmas.summary: Ordinary induction on an explicit upper bound implements constructive strong descent through a proper factor.

peano.statement: forall B n. (exists t. t + n = B) -> ~(n = 0) -> ~(n = 1) -> exists p. ((~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1) /\ exists k. n = p * k)

lemmas.title: Every nontrivial natural has a prime divisor
lemmas.summary: Instantiating bounded prime search at the number itself constructs an expanded prime predicate and an explicit divisibility witness.

peano.statement: forall n. ~(n = 0) -> ~(n = 1) -> exists p. ((~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1) /\ exists k. n = p * k)

lemmas.title: Every divisor of a prime is one or the prime
lemmas.summary: Every divisor of a prime is one or the prime itself.

peano.statement: forall p g. (~(p = 1) /\ forall c d. p = c * d -> c = 1 \/ d = 1) -> (exists x. p = g * x) -> g = 1 \/ p = g

lemmas.title: Euclid's lemma
lemmas.summary: A prime dividing a product divides at least one factor (Euclid's lemma).

peano.statement: forall p a b. (~(p = 1) /\ forall c d. p = c * d -> c = 1 \/ d = 1) -> (exists k. a * b = p * k) -> (exists u. a = p * u) \/ exists v. b = p * v

lemmas.title: There is a prime larger than every given natural
lemmas.summary: Euclid's common-multiple argument constructively produces a prime strictly above every natural.

peano.statement: forall n. exists p. (exists k. k + S n = p) /\ (~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1)

lemmas.title: A product of two primes is unique up to order
lemmas.summary: A fixed-length factorization theorem that fits today's term language and exercises Euclid's lemma.

peano.statement: forall p q r s. (~(p = 1) /\ forall a b. p = a * b -> a = 1 \/ b = 1) -> (~(q = 1) /\ forall c d. q = c * d -> c = 1 \/ d = 1) -> (~(r = 1) /\ forall e f. r = e * f -> e = 1 \/ f = 1) -> (~(s = 1) /\ forall g h. s = g * h -> g = 1 \/ h = 1) -> p * q = r * s -> (p = r /\ q = s) \/ (p = s /\ q = r)

lemmas.title: Every Gödel-beta modulus is nonzero
lemmas.summary: Records constructively that the decoding modulus 1 + (i + 1)c is a successor.

peano.statement: forall c i. ~(S ((S i) * c) = 0)

lemmas.title: A bounded value is its own Gödel-beta residue
lemmas.summary: Constructs a one-position decoding witness with quotient zero whenever the proposed value is below the modulus.

peano.statement: forall c i x. (exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) -> ((exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. x = q * S ((S i) * c) + x)

lemmas.title: Every Gödel-beta position has a decoded value
lemmas.summary: Uses quotient-remainder existence at modulus 1 + (i + 1)c and retains both the bound and quotient witnesses.

peano.statement: forall b c i. exists x. ((exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + x)

lemmas.title: A Gödel-beta decoded value is unique
lemmas.summary: Reduces two expanded beta-value witnesses at the same code and position to uniqueness of quotient and remainder.

peano.statement: forall b c i x y. ((exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + x) -> ((exists h. h + S y = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + y) -> x = y

lemmas.title: Every Gödel-beta position has exactly one decoded value
lemmas.summary: Packages beta-value totality and functionality into a single expanded first-order theorem.

peano.statement: forall b c i. exists x. (((exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + x) /\ forall y. ((exists h. h + S y = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + y) -> x = y)

lemmas.title: A Gödel-beta value is congruent to its code
lemmas.summary: Projects the directed quotient witness from an expanded beta value and exposes it through the balanced congruence API.

peano.statement: forall b c i x. ((exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + x) -> exists u v. b + S ((S i) * c) * u = x + S ((S i) * c) * v

lemmas.title: A bounded congruent value is a Gödel-beta value
lemmas.summary: Uses nonzeroness of the beta modulus and the reverse remainder bridge to reconstruct the directed decoding witness.

peano.statement: forall b c i x. (exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) -> (exists u v. b + S ((S i) * c) * u = x + S ((S i) * c) * v) -> ((exists h. h + S x = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. b = q * S ((S i) * c) + x)

lemmas.title: A single Gödel-beta code realizes two bounded values
lemmas.summary: Specializes constructive binary CRT to two pairwise coprime beta moduli and reconstructs both expanded BetaAt witnesses from their bounds and congruences.

peano.statement: forall c i j a b. (forall d. (exists u. S ((S i) * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. S ((S j) * c) = d * v) -> d = 1) -> (exists ha. ha + S a = S ((S i) * c)) -> (exists hb. hb + S b = S ((S j) * c)) -> exists code. (((exists ha. ha + S a = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. code = q * S ((S i) * c) + a) /\ ((exists hb. hb + S b = S ((S j) * c)) /\ exists r. code = r * S ((S j) * c) + b))

lemmas.title: A Gödel-beta modulus is coprime to its base
lemmas.summary: A common divisor of c and the successor modulus 1 + kc divides the remainder one and is therefore one.

peano.statement: forall c k d. (exists u. S (k * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. c = d * v) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: A common beta-modulus divisor divides the scaled index gap
lemmas.summary: When j is i plus an explicit gap, every common divisor of their beta moduli divides gap times c.

peano.statement: forall c i j gap d. j = i + gap -> (exists u. S ((S i) * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. S ((S j) * c) = d * v) -> exists w. gap * c = d * w

lemmas.title: Divisible index gaps give coprime Gödel-beta moduli
lemmas.summary: If the additive index gap divides c, Gauss cancellation turns the scaled-gap divisibility result into pairwise coprimality of the beta moduli.

peano.statement: forall c i j gap. j = i + gap -> (exists k. c = gap * k) -> forall d. (exists u. S ((S i) * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. S ((S j) * c) = d * v) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: A divisible index gap supplies a two-position Gödel-beta code
lemmas.summary: Discharges the beta-pair CRT coprimality premise from an explicit additive gap that divides c, yielding one code for both bounded values.

peano.statement: forall c i j gap a b. j = i + gap -> (exists k. c = gap * k) -> (exists ha. ha + S a = S ((S i) * c)) -> (exists hb. hb + S b = S ((S j) * c)) -> exists code. (((exists ha. ha + S a = S ((S i) * c)) /\ exists q. code = q * S ((S i) * c) + a) /\ ((exists hb. hb + S b = S ((S j) * c)) /\ exists r. code = r * S ((S j) * c) + b))

lemmas.title: Ordered bounded Gödel-beta moduli are coprime
lemmas.summary: For ordered indices within a common-multiple bound, the positive index gap divides c and therefore supplies coprime beta moduli.

peano.statement: forall B c i j. (forall t. (exists h. S t + S h = S B) -> exists k. c = S t * k) -> (exists g. g + S i = j) -> (exists h. h + j = B) -> forall d. (exists u. S ((S i) * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. S ((S j) * c) = d * v) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: A bounded Gödel-beta prefix has pairwise coprime moduli
lemmas.summary: Trichotomy orients any two distinct bounded indices and reduces their modulus coprimality to the ordered-gap theorem.

peano.statement: forall B c. (forall t. (exists h. S t + S h = S B) -> exists k. c = S t * k) -> forall i j. ~(i = j) -> (exists hi. hi + i = B) -> (exists hj. hj + j = B) -> forall d. (exists u. S ((S i) * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. S ((S j) * c) = d * v) -> d = 1

lemmas.title: Every finite Gödel-beta prefix admits a pairwise-coprime base
lemmas.summary: The bounded common-multiple construction supplies a nonzero c for which every two distinct beta moduli in the requested finite prefix are coprime.

peano.statement: forall B. exists c. (~(c = 0) /\ forall i j. ~(i = j) -> (exists hi. hi + i = B) -> (exists hj. hj + j = B) -> forall d. (exists u. S ((S i) * c) = d * u) -> (exists v. S ((S j) * c) = d * v) -> d = 1)

lemmas.summary: Multiplying the accumulated product by the next beta modulus preserves nonzeroness, divisibility by all earlier moduli, and coprimality with every future bounded modulus.

P = S ((S i) * c) * q) -> (forall j. (exists g. g + S k = j) -> (exists h. h + j = N) -> forall d. (exists u. P = d * u) -> (exists v.
